title: Delegated Access Simulator and Authorization Middleware for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Customers and internal admins frequently need to predict how RBAC v2 policy changes will affect access paths across service boundaries (API/runtime/console). We lack a safe, observable way to stage policy changes for delegated admin roles and to propagate SAML session attributes into policy evaluation. This ticket builds a simulator and lightweight authorization middleware that can run in 'dry-run' mode (simulate decisions and produce enriched audit events) and in 'enforce' mode for gradual rollout. The work covers: (1) evaluation engine adapter that accepts expanded request context (SAML attributes, session_id, delegation_chain), (2) a middleware shim for API/runtime/console that can toggle simulate vs enforce, (3) an enriched audit event schema for simulated decisions and attribute diffs, and (4) a canary rollout plan with rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator API that takes a request payload and returns allow/deny verdict plus decision trace and score (latency <50ms P50 for single-eval),
Middleware implemented as a minimal sidecar/filter for API gateway and console backend with feature flag to toggle simulate/enforce per route,
Audit events emitted for both simulated and enforced decisions to the audit pipeline with new fields: simulated:boolean, decision_trace_url, session_attributes_hash, delegation_chain,
SAML session attributes (e.g., eduPersonScopedAffiliation, groups, external_org_role) are available to policy engine and correctly interpolated into policy variables,
End-to-end tests covering delegated admin use-cases (grant via role, deny on missing attr, fallback to admin-override) with test coverage >85% for new modules,

Canary rollout configured: 5% of traffic simulated for one week, automatic metrics check (errors/access regressions) and auto rollback if any high-severity mismatch or latency regression (>15% P99 increase),
Security review completed and sign-off from security and privacy teams before full enforce rollout.
design_notes: Policy language: reuse existing RBAC v2 AST but add first-class support for session attributes and delegation_chain[] tuple,

Evaluation engine: keep deterministic evaluator; add a trace mode that records matched rules, matched principals, and cache keys; store a concise decision_trace (<=4KB) pointing to full trace in object store for heavy traces,
Middleware: design as two small components - a request enrich step (inject session attrs + provenance) and a decision adapter that calls evaluation engine with timeout guard 150ms,

Audit schema: new top-level fields 'simulated' and 'simulated_reason'; include attribute_hash to allow customers to query identical sessions without leaking raw PII; events should be JSONL compliant and routed to existing audit pipeline,
Caching: cache allow/deny results keyed by (policy_version, principal_id, resource_id, action, attrs_hash) with 30s TTL; simulator must bypass caching when ?force_sim=true,
Fallback: on eval timeout or engine error, middleware follows configured fallback_policy: 'deny-by-default' for enforce, 'record-unknown' for simulate,
Performance: expect <5% P50 latency increase on API gateway when middleware in simulate mode; optimise by async emit of audit events and local short-circuit for common allow rules.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Integration tests and internal dev-preview with synthetic SAML assertions (dev cluster),
Phase 1: Deploy simulator middleware to staging and run a 24h smoke with 1000 synthetic requests verifying decision parity and audit schema,
Phase 2: Canary simulate on 5% production traffic for 7 days; surface mismatch metrics and session attribute coverage dashboards,
Phase 3: Expand simulate to 25% and run A/B compare of error rates, latency, and false-positive rate on delegated admin flows,
Phase 4: After approval and security sign-off, flip feature flag to 'enforce' for low-risk namespaces and monitor for 48h,
Phase 5: Gradual global enforce rollout with team-run checkpoints and rollback playbook.
test_plan: Unit: evaluator trace generation and rule-matching permutations,
Integration: middleware + SAML session propagation using local OIDC/SAML test IdP,
E2E: delegated admin scenarios across API, runtime, and console where a single policy change should update behavior in all three surfaces,
Load: synthetic load test hitting policy engine at 1000rps to validate 99th percentile latency under cache hit/miss scenarios,
Security: fuzz SAML attributes and injection attempts to ensure attribute parsing and hashing are safe,
Compliance: verify audit events contain non-PII hashes and meet retention/format expectations.
monitoring: New dashboard: 'RBAC v2 Simulator Health' - evaluation rate, simulated_vs_enforced ratio, simulated_mismatch_rate, avg_decision_latency P50/P95/P99,
Alert: simulated_mismatch_rate > 0.5% for 1h high -> pulse to security/product,
Alert: eval P99 > 200ms -> automatic traffic diversion to fallback path,
Audit delivery metric: % of audit events successfully delivered to pipeline within 30s,
Canary comparison metrics: delegated_admin_access_error_delta and console-login-regression.
open_questions: Which attributes from the SAML assertion are allowed to be used in policy (privacy constraints)? We should publish an allow-list,
Do we need a separate enrollment flow to opt delegated admins into simulation vs enforced? Could be per-organization setting in Console,
Should simulated decisions be visible to end-customer tenants in their audit UI or only to internal admins? Consider access controls and PII,
What is the maximum size of decision_trace we want to persist in object store before truncation? Default plan: 4KB inline, full trace in S3-like store.
dependencies_notes: Requires RBAC v2 policy indexer changes to emit policy_version header (ENG-21456),
Needs gateway feature-flag infra for per-route simulate/enforce toggles (ENG-11820),
Audit pipeline schema change coordinated with data-platform team and compliance.
